frontier.hypothesis: A directed/randomized permuter on a clean single-function target closes the coupled sched1/RA fixpoint that structural transforms provably cannot.
frontier.mechanism: The target sits at a scheduler+allocator fixpoint {base->$a1, var_v0->$v0, partial-before-reload}. sched1 deterministically front-loads the arg0 reload in every single-basic-block structural form; a permuter search over the mutation space (incl. non-dataflow-preserving spellings the manual sweep won't try) may perturb sched1's load-hoist / register pressure into the fixpoint.

NON-structural modality.

frontier.hypothesis: A scheduling-technique lever (NOT structural reassociation) can suppress sched1's front-load of the arg0 reload without changing dataflow, keeping the partial-add before it.
frontier.mechanism: The 43rd nop survives only if the reload is NOT hoisted above the partial-add. The hoist is a load-latency-hiding priority boost; suppressing it needs a scheduling-level effect (e.g. a sanctioned do-while(0)/LABEL_OUTSIDE_LOOP_P / reorg-level interaction) rather than an add-side rewrite. Arm-duplication achieves the block boundary but is defeated by cross-jump's per-arm base-reg divergence.
frontier.next_probe: Investigate whether a sanctioned do-while(0) wrapper or a reorg-level (relax_delay_slots / .dbr) effect can keep the reload after the partial-add; check .dbr/.sched dump behavior. Verify any wrapper against the do-while-zero-exception prerequisites. Separate (scheduling-technique) modality.
